W3 (cost lens), after E020.

**Current tip (E017 code).** Muon on the conv filters (3 Newton-Schulz steps, filters renormalized every step, so filter weight decay is inert). Lookahead/EMA. Resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps. Batch 2000, widths 128/384/512, label smoothing 0.3, SGD-group wd 0.006, 9.5 true epochs (~238 steps), max-autotune with CUDA graphs. Measured 6.548 s at 0.7537; the E019 rerun gave 6.540 s at 0.7541. The same build reproduces to within about 0.05 pp. E016's 0.7607 at identical math was a kernel/trajectory reshuffle. My estimate of the true mean is about 0.754–0.755.

**Time budget:** time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction, with F ≈ 0.6 s, V ≈ 7.8 s and pixel fraction ≈ 0.755.
- Systems levers are exhausted (E015, E017).
- Lower-resolution steps save a bit more than pixel-proportional (E011, E018 under-predicted).
- Per-sample conv MACs at 32 px: group 1 ≈ 93M (conv3 ≈ 33M, 7%), group 2 ≈ 230M (51%), group 3 ≈ 129M.
- Narrowing group 2 to 320 removes about 70M MACs (≈15.6%), counting group 3's first conv.

**Exchange rates (time per pp of accuracy), with E020 as the new information:**
- Epochs: E020 cut 1.0 true epoch (−10.5% time, −0.69 s) for only −0.1 pp against the E017/E019 reproduction (≈0.754). Its 0.7528 just missed 0.753. That is about 7 s/pp, far cheaper than the 2 s/pp I assumed, though one 3-seed difference has an SE of about 0.25 pp. Epochs now look like the cheapest dial, and a −0.5 epoch point (≈6.2 s) is the obvious next feasible candidate.
- Last-group width: 1.6 s/pp (E010).
- Dropping the 28 px phase: 1.6 s/pp (E018).
- 20 px aggressive schedule: about 0.9 s/pp (E011).
- So architecture and resolution trims look worse than epoch trims. That is the opposite of H2.5's premise.

**Mechanisms:**
1. Lookahead endpoint averaging is worth about +1 pp (E005).
2. Muon gives about +0.66 pp (E006).
3. Accuracy is built across the mid- and high-resolution phases; removing resolution hurts more than its pixel share suggests (E011, E018).
4. CIFAR-100 is width-hungry (E010).
5. Hyperparameter nudges (label smoothing, Muon lr, wd) are all inside noise (E013, E014, E016/E017).
6. Kernel selection can move the 3-seed mean by up to about 0.7 pp at identical math (E016 vs E017).

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp.
- A rebuild with new kernel choices can shift the mean more.
- Time noise is about 0.5–1%.

**Unsure:**
- Whether E020's flat slope is real or a lucky draw.
- The 40-seed PCIe mean (≈0.754, fine against 0.75).
- How efficient tensor cores are at 320 channels.
- Whether depth in group 1 matters for CIFAR-100.

forecasts.reason: Removes about 15% of MACs, roughly −8% time. Width-hungry CIFAR-100 likely loses 0.3–0.5 pp, which is worse than E020's epoch-trim exchange rate.
Weight-decay nudges have stayed inside noise. +0.2 pp over E016's reshuffled 0.7607 is very unlikely.
About 7% of MACs plus the largest-map elementwise traffic gives roughly −7% time, likely just short of −8%. Losing depth probably costs about 0.4 pp.
Pixel fraction drops only 0.755 to 0.729, about −0.25 s (≈4%, right at the threshold). The accuracy cost is small but within noise of the 0.25 pp limit.

cruxes: Is E020's near-flat epoch slope (−1 epoch, −0.1 pp) real? A −0.5 epoch run (≈6.2 s) or seeds 3–12 at both 9.5 and 8.5 epochs would settle it. If it is real, epoch trims beat every architecture or resolution trim.
Does narrowing group 2 to 320 save time in proportion to its MACs (≈−8% or more), or do tensor-core and memory effects shrink the gain?
Is there any accuracy lever that beats noise by at least 0.3 pp (BN-stat recompute after the EMA swap, a longer EMA) to fund a cut of 0.5–1 epoch below 0.753?
